# Active Members {#active-members}

**XX** out of **XX**  members are active on Collaboratory, which is  **XX%**  of the community. 

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

# Filter to last 3 months (~12 weeks)
active_kpi_plot <- kpi_weekly %>%
  arrange(week) %>%
  filter(week >= max(week) - 84)

# Plot
ggplot(active_kpi_plot, aes(x = week, y = prop_active_90d)) +
  geom_line(color = "#212752", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#212752", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Active Members",
    subtitle = glue("As of {format(max(active_kpi_plot$week), '%d %B %Y')}"),
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    expand = expansion(add = c(7, 7))  # extend left/right
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, family = "Lato", color = "#2F3E46", face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, face = "italic", family = "Lato", color = "#2F3E46"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```

# Engagement {#engagement}

Monthly engagement metrics provide an overview of user activity on the forum. These include total and new user counts, along with averages for user activity.Users are classified by recency of activity:

-   **Active**: last seen within 30 days
-   **Dormant**: last seen 31–60 days ago
-   **Uninterested**: last seen more than 60 days ago

Engagement intensity is assessed based on the average time a user spends reading per month, normalized by account age, enabling comparison across all users. Based on this measure, users are categorized as:

-   **Highly Engaged**: 15 or more minutes per month
-   **Moderately Engaged**: between 2 and 15 minutes per month
-   **Barely Engaged**: less than 2 minutes per month

::: panel-tabset
### Engagement Metrics {#engagement-metrics}

All figures reflect month-over-month changes to support interpretation of longer-term trends. Note that the monthly change for activity and engagement reflects increases or decreases in absolute numbers, and does not indicate changes in their proportional share of the user base.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
metrics_table %>%
  kbl(format = "html", align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
, escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    font_size = 15
  ) %>%
  column_spec(1, width = "16em", bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "12em") %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "12em") %>%
  column_spec(4, width = "12em", 
              color = dplyr::case_when(
                grepl("-", metrics_table$`Monthly Change`) ~ "#d33c32",
                grepl("\\d", metrics_table$`Monthly Change`) ~ "#007e3a",
                TRUE ~ "black"
              )
  )%>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2f3e46")
```

# Engagement Levels

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
# Step 1: Convert wide to long, calculate ratios per week
engagement_long <- engagement_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Category,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "Users"
  ) %>%
  mutate(week = as.Date(week)) %>%
  group_by(week) %>%
  mutate(
    total_users = sum(Users, na.rm = TRUE),
    ratio = Users / total_users
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Filter last 3 months (~84 days) of data
engagement_recent <- engagement_long %>%
  filter(week >= max(week) - 84)

# Step 3: Clean category names and set factor levels
engagement_recent <- engagement_recent %>%
  mutate(
    Category = recode(Category,
      "Barely engaged (under 2 min/month)" = "Barely engaged",
      "Moderately engaged (2-15 min/month)" = "Moderately engaged",
      "Highly engaged (15+ min/month)" = "Highly engaged"
    ),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = c(
      "Barely engaged", "Moderately engaged", "Highly engaged"
    ))
  )

# Step 4: Line chart
line_chart <- ggplot(engagement_recent, aes(x = week, y = ratio, color = Category)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Engagement Levels – Over Time",
    subtitle = glue("As of {format(max(engagement_recent$week), '%d %B %Y')}"),
    x = "", y = ""
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    expand = expansion(add = c(7, 7))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Barely engaged" = "#212752",
      "Moderately engaged" = "#4595CF",
      "Highly engaged" = "#E9AC3B"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, family = "Lato", color = "#2F3E46", face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, face = "italic", family = "Lato", color = "#2F3E46"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Step 5: Pie chart for latest week
latest_week <- max(engagement_recent$week)

engagement_latest <- engagement_recent %>%
  filter(week == latest_week) %>%
  mutate(
    label = glue("{Category}\n{scales::percent(ratio, accuracy = 1)}")
  )

pie_chart <- ggplot(engagement_latest, aes(x = "", y = ratio, fill = Category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  labs(title = "Engagement Levels – Latest Week") +
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
   "Barely engaged" = "#212752",
      "Moderately engaged" = "#4595CF",
      "Highly engaged" = "#E9AC3B"
    )
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.7, color = "white") +
  theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    size = 14,
    face = "bold",
    hjust = 0.5,
    family = "Lato",
    color = "#2F3E46"
  ),
  legend.position = "none",
  plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
)

# Step 6: Show plots side-by-side
gridExtra::grid.arrange(line_chart, pie_chart, ncol = 2, widths = c(1.2, 0.8))
```
